entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # AG urges High Court to strike down law freezing arrest of Haredi draft dodgers. ## Gali Baharav-Miara says controversial legislation is 'discriminatory' and 'an extreme and clear case of harmful legislation that does not meet legal standards'. Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara urged the High Court on Friday to overturn legislation freezing the arrest of ultra-Orthodox draft dodgers. Submitting the state’s opinion, Baharav-Miara called the law passed during a final legislative blitz by the government earlier this month “an extreme and clear case of flawed and harmful legislation that does not meet legal standards.”. Several petitions were filed against the law immediately after its passage, arguing that the legislation was discriminatory since it bans arrests for ultra-Orthodox yeshiva students who have failed to obey conscription orders, while allowing arrests for non-Haredi draft dodgers to continue. The court has already temporarily frozen the implementation of the law and Baharav-Miara urged the court to block it completely.

Griffin’s office had filed an emergency petition with the high court in May, after a Pulaski County judge did not immediately grant his motion to approve the settlement and end his suit against the Arkansas Board of Corrections. Under the settlement, the board is required to admit to three violations of the Arkansas Freedom of Information Act and commit to complying with the public records law in the future.
